- **Limitations:** May not achieve the same level of temporal consistency as methods that explicitly track features over time, though it avoids their high computational cost [S1].

The claim states that the method may not achieve the same level of temporal consistency as methods that explicitly track features, but avoids their high computational cost. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly contrasts the proposed method with methods that 'track features over time to generate a temporally consistent mesh connectivity and UV parametrization,' noting that the latter process is 'expensive and cannot be applied to real-time applications.' It further states that the proposed method 'encourages temporal consistency without tracking.' While the text claims the method 'encourages' consistency, the context of comparing it against the 'expensive' tracking methods supports the implication that it is a trade-off (avoiding cost/expensiveness) compared to the explicit tracking methods. The specific phrasing 'may not achieve the same level' is a reasonable inference from the distinction made between 'encouraging' consistency without tracking versus the explicit, expensive tracking methods, and the evidence supports the core facts: it avoids tracking and the associated high cost/expensiveness.
